title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
authors: Jenny Zhang; Shengran Hu; Cong Lu; Robert Lange; Jeff Clune
tldr: Keeps an archive of coding agents that rewrite their own source and validates each variant empirically on benchmarks instead of proving it better, branching from whatever survives.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Trains long reasoning with rule-based correctness rewards, then recycles the best sampled traces into supervised data for the next round - a verifier-driven loop with no learned reward model.

title: A Survey on Data Selection for Language Models
authors: Alon Albalak; Yanai Elazar; Sang Michael Xie; Shayne Longpre; Nathan Lambert; Xinyi Wang; Niklas Muennighoff; Bairu Hou; Liangming Pan; Haewon Jeong; et al.
tldr: Organises data selection for language models into one pipeline vocabulary, covering filtering, deduplication, mixing and selection objectives across pretraining and fine-tuning.

title: Data Selection for Language Models via Importance Resampling
authors: Sang Michael Xie; Shibani Santurkar; Tengyu Ma; Percy Liang
tldr: Selects pretraining text by importance resampling against a target distribution in n-gram feature space, making "what belongs in this corpus" a cheap, tunable decision.

title: Data-Juicer: A One-Stop Data Processing System for Large Language Models
authors: Daoyuan Chen; Yilun Huang; Zhijian Ma; Hesen Chen; Xuchen Pan; Ce Ge; Dawei Gao; Yuexiang Xie; Zhaoyang Liu; Jinyang Gao; et al.
tldr: Provides a composable operator library and recipe format for cleaning, deduplicating and mixing LLM corpora, so a data pipeline becomes a versioned artefact instead of a one-off script.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
authors: Hunter Lightman; Vineet Kosaraju; Yura Burda; Harri Edwards; Bowen Baker; Teddy Lee; Jan Leike; John Schulman; Ilya Sutskever; Karl Cobbe
tldr: Compares outcome against process supervision on math and finds step-level reward models, trained on 800K human step labels, pick correct solutions far more reliably.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
authors: Carlos E. Jimenez; John Yang; Alexander Wettig; Shunyu Yao; Kexin Pei; Ofir Press; Karthik Narasimhan
tldr: Turns real GitHub issues and their merged fixes into an execution-verified task suite, giving self-improving code loops a ground truth that is expensive to game.

title: The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget
authors: Ilia Shumailov; Zakhar Shumaylov; Yiren Zhao; Yarin Gal; Nicolas Papernot; Ross Anderson
tldr: Shows that training generation after generation on model output erodes the tails of the distribution first, so a closed synthetic loop forgets rare events before it degrades on average.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
authors: Guanzhi Wang; Yuqi Xie; Yunfan Jiang; Ajay Mandlekar; Chaowei Xiao; Yuke Zhu; Linxi Fan; Anima Anandkumar
tldr: Runs a lifelong Minecraft agent that proposes its own curriculum and stores every verified program as a reusable skill, improving through a growing library rather than a weight update.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
authors: Yuntao Bai; Saurav Kadavath; Sandipan Kundu; Amanda Askell; Jackson Kernion; Andy Jones; Anna Chen; Anna Goldie; Azalia Mirhoseini; Cameron McKinnon; et al.
tldr: Replaces human harmlessness labels with a written constitution: the model critiques and revises its own answers, then a preference model is trained on those AI-authored comparisons.

title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
authors: Yizhong Wang; Yeganeh Kordi; Swaroop Mishra; Alisa Liu; Noah A. Smith; Daniel Khashabi; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
tldr: Bootstraps an instruction-tuning corpus out of a base model itself, sampling new tasks from a small human seed pool and filtering near-duplicates before fine-tuning on what survives.

title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
authors: Eric Zelikman; Yuhuai Wu; Jesse Mu; Noah D. Goodman
tldr: Keeps only the self-generated rationales that reach the known answer, fine-tunes on them and repeats, turning answer checking into a renewable supply of reasoning traces.

title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions
authors: Rui Wang; Joel Lehman; Jeff Clune; Kenneth O. Stanley
tldr: Co-evolves a population of agents together with the obstacle courses that challenge them, transferring solutions between niches so the task distribution keeps outrunning the solvers.

title: Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge
authors: David Silver; Julian Schrittwieser; Karen Simonyan; Ioannis Antonoglou; Aja Huang; Arthur Guez; Thomas Hubert; Lucas Baker; Matthew Lai; Adrian Bolton; et al.
tldr: Learns Go from random play by treating its own tree search as the teacher, evidence that a self-play data loop with no human games can overtake systems trained on them.
